headline.purpose: The E-STOP label, and nothing else. The largest type anywhere in the system.

title.purpose: Brand lockup, robot names, group headers, button labels. The workhorse for anything clickable or nameable.

body.purpose: Base reading size. Help text drops to 12px / 1.5 with a 62ch measure.

label.purpose: Eyebrows and section markers in Etched Grey, tracked to 0.22em so they read as engraving on a panel.

readout.purpose: Any quantity a robot reported or a validator clamped: telemetry, coordinates, config numbers, node ids.

micro.purpose: The smallest legible unit — axis rows, map tags, bind values, graph edge labels.

shadows.name: panel-float
shadows.purpose: Every floating glass panel. The inset line is a machined bevel catching light.

shadows.name: pad-float
shadows.purpose: The drive pad — slightly heavier, as the object closest to the operator.

shadows.name: sheet-lift
shadows.purpose: The bottom-sheet rail in portrait, casting its shadow upward.

shadows.name: cap
shadows.purpose: Raised physical caps lit from above: the drive nub and the range-slider thumb.

shadows.name: alarm
shadows.purpose: The e-stop's red bloom. Animates to '0 10px 42px -4px rgba(255,60,76,0.95)' on the armed pulse.

shadows.name: led-glow
shadows.purpose: A lit indicator — status LEDs, online dots (9px), calibration pips (6px). Only ever on something live.

shadows.name: status-gutter
shadows.purpose: A field's left-edge state bar. Amber dirty, green confirmed, red rejected, blue listening.

shadows.name: leaflet-bar
shadows.purpose: Map zoom controls, themed to match the panel vocabulary.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: Default easing for state changes — press, toggle, tab, chevron. Real-world mass; never linear or ease-in-out.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: Things settling into place: the drive nub returning to center, the settings sheet rising, a map arrow rotating.

motion.name: duration-data
motion.purpose: Live measurements only — telemetry bars, axis fills. Linear because easing a measurement misreports the machine.

motion.name: duration-control
motion.purpose: Button press, icon-button, input focus, tab switch.

motion.name: duration-sheet
motion.purpose: The portrait rail drawer sliding to and from collapsed.

motion.name: estop-pulse
motion.purpose: The armed e-stop breathing. Also the cadence of the controller 'listening for input' fade.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Global kill switch under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce. Applied with !important to *.

components.name: Glass Panel
components.description: The floating instrument surface. Every piece of HUD chrome is one of these, laid over the live map.
components.html:
Fleet
Instruments float; the terrain shows through.
components.css: .ds-panel { position: relative; background: var(--panel, rgba(19,24,33,0.72)); border: 1px solid var(--hairline, rgba(255,255,255,0.08)); border-radius: var(--radius, 20px); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.06), 0 18px 50px -24px rgba(0,0,0,0.8); backdrop-filter: blur(20px) saturate(1.3); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(20px) saturate(1.3); padding: 14px; color: var(--text, #e9edf4); font-family: var(--font-ui, 'Space Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-panel-eyebrow { display: block; font-size: 10px; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.22em; color: var(--faint, #5c6675); } .ds-panel-body { margin-top: 8px; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.4; }

components.name: Button
components.description: The default control: raised glass, 52px tap floor, compresses on press.
components.css: .ds-btn { appearance: none; font-family: var(--font-ui, 'Space Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.01em; color: var(--text, #e9edf4); background: var(--panel-2, rgba(31,38,48,0.7)); border: 1px solid var(--hairline, rgba(255,255,255,0.08)); border-radius: var(--radius-sm, 13px); min-height: 52px; padding: 0 15px; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.06); transition: transform 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1), background 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1), border-color 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1), color 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1); } .ds-btn:focus-visible { outline: none; border-color: var(--accent, #4c9eff); } .ds-btn:active { transform: scale(0.96); }

components.name: Button — Active
components.description: The selected mode or on-state. The strongest inversion in the system: Beacon Blue fill with near-black ink.
components.css: .ds-btn-active { appearance: none; font-family: var(--font-ui, 'Space Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.01em; color: var(--on-accent, #06131f); background: var(--accent, #4c9eff); border: 1px solid var(--accent, #4c9eff); border-radius: var(--radius-sm, 13px); min-height: 52px; padding: 0 15px; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.06); transition: transform 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1); } .ds-btn-active:active { transform: scale(0.96); }

components.name: Button — Danger
components.description: A destructive action. Washed red at rest; commits to a full red fill the instant it is pressed.
components.css: .ds-btn-danger { appearance: none; font-family: var(--font-ui, 'Space Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 15px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--danger, #ff4d5a); background: rgba(255,77,90,0.1); border: 1px solid rgba(255,77,90,0.4); border-radius: var(--radius-sm, 13px); min-height: 52px; padding: 0 15px; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.06); transition: transform 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1), background 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1), color 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1); } .ds-btn-danger:active { transform: scale(0.96); background: var(--danger, #ff4d5a); color: #fff; }

components.name: E-STOP
components.description: The single most important object on screen. The only large saturated fill in the system; breathes when a robot is latched.
components.css: .ds-estop { font-family: var(--font-ui, 'Space Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); font-weight: 700; font-size: 17px; letter-spacing: 0.14em; color: #fff; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #ff5b67, #e0313e); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.2); border-radius: 16px; min-height: 60px; padding: 0 26px; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 10px 30px -8px rgba(255,60,76,0.6), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.06); transition: transform 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1), box-shadow 0.2s cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1); } .ds-estop:active { transform: scale(0.95); } .ds-estop.ds-armed { animation: ds-estop-pulse 1.1s cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1) infinite; } @keyframes ds-estop-pulse { 0%, 100% { box-shadow: 0 10px 30px -8px rgba(255,60,76,0.55), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.06); } 50% { box-shadow: 0 10px 42px -4px rgba(255,60,76,0.95), inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.06); } } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-estop.ds-armed { animation-duration: 0.001ms; } }

components.name: Robot Card
components.description: One robot in the fleet rail. The 1.5px border is present but transparent at rest, so selecting never reflows the list.
components.css: .ds-robot { padding: 12px 13px; border-radius: var(--radius-sm, 13px); background: var(--panel-2, rgba(31,38,48,0.7)); border: 1.5px solid transparent; cursor: pointer; color: var(--text, #e9edf4); font-family: var(--font-ui, 'Space Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); transition: border-color 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1), transform 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1), background 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1); } .ds-robot:active { transform: scale(0.985); } .ds-robot.ds-sel { border-color: var(--accent, #4c9eff); background: rgba(76,158,255,0.1); } .ds-robot-top { display: flex; align-items: center; justify-content: space-between; } .ds-robot-name { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 9px; font-weight: 600; font-size: 16px; } .ds-dot { width: 10px; height: 10px; border-radius: 50%; background: var(--ok, #35c46b); box-shadow: 0 0 9px var(--ok, #35c46b); flex: none; } .ds-robot-mode { font-size: 12px; color: var(--muted, #8b95a5); font-variant: small-caps; letter-spacing: 0.04em; } .ds-robot-meta { display: flex; gap: 15px; margin-top: 7px; font-size: 12.5px; color: var(--muted, #8b95a5); font-family: var(--font-mono, 'JetBrains Mono Variable', ui-monospace, monospace); }

components.name: Number Field
components.description: A tunable, recessed into a well. The left-edge gutter reports whether the edit is pending, confirmed, or refused by the robot.
components.html:
Align P gain kp

Clamped by the robot, then echoed back.
components.css: .ds-field { padding: 11px 0; border-bottom: 1px solid var(--hairline, rgba(255,255,255,0.08)); font-family: var(--font-ui, 'Space Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); } .ds-field.ds-dirty { box-shadow: inset 2px 0 0 var(--warn, #f0a53a); padding-left: 10px; } .ds-field-head { display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 10px; min-height: 34px; } .ds-field-label { flex: 1; font-size: 14.5px; font-weight: 500; color: var(--text, #e9edf4); display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 8px; } .ds-field-unit { color: var(--faint, #5c6675); font-family: var(--font-mono, 'JetBrains Mono Variable', ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 11.5px; } .ds-field-num { appearance: none; -moz-appearance: textfield; font-family: var(--font-mono, 'JetBrains Mono Variable', ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 14px; color: var(--text, #e9edf4); background: #0c0f15; border: 1px solid var(--hairline, rgba(255,255,255,0.08)); border-radius: 10px; min-height: 38px; width: 92px; text-align: right; padding: 0 10px; flex: none; } .ds-field-num::-webkit-outer-spin-button, .ds-field-num::-webkit-inner-spin-button { appearance: none; margin: 0; } .ds-field-num:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--accent, #4c9eff); } .ds-field-help { font-size: 12px; line-height: 1.5; color: var(--muted, #8b95a5); margin: 4px 0 0; max-width: 62ch; }

components.name: Status Pill
components.description: A lozenge-shaped indicator lamp. The LED inside carries the signal color so the text can stay quiet.
components.css: .ds-pill { display: inline-flex; align-items: center; gap: 7px; font-family: var(--font-mono, 'JetBrains Mono Variable', ui-monospace, monospace); font-size: 11.5px; font-weight: 600; letter-spacing: 0.02em; padding: 6px 13px; border-radius: 999px; background: var(--panel-2, rgba(31,38,48,0.7)); color: var(--muted, #8b95a5); border: 1px solid var(--hairline, rgba(255,255,255,0.08)); white-space: nowrap; } .ds-led { width: 8px; height: 8px; border-radius: 50%; background: currentColor; box-shadow: 0 0 8px currentColor; flex: none; } .ds-led-ok { color: var(--ok, #35c46b); }

components.name: Toggle
components.description: A 56x32 well that fills Beacon Blue when on; the knob translates 24px and brightens to pure white.
components.css: .ds-toggle { appearance: none; position: relative; width: 56px; height: 32px; flex: none; border-radius: 999px; background: #0c0f15; border: 1px solid var(--hairline, rgba(255,255,255,0.08)); cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.28s cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1), border-color 0.28s cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1); } .ds-toggle.ds-on { background: var(--accent, #4c9eff); border-color: var(--accent, #4c9eff); } .ds-knob { position: absolute; top: 3px; left: 3px; width: 24px; height: 24px; border-radius: 50%; background: #cdd7e4; box-shadow: 0 2px 6px rgba(0,0,0,0.6); transition: transform 0.28s cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1); } .ds-toggle.ds-on .ds-knob { transform: translateX(24px); background: #fff; }

components.name: Tab Strip
components.description: The only navigation in the system, inside the settings sheet. The active tab reads as raised out of the well it sits in.
components.css: .ds-tabs { display: inline-flex; gap: 4px; padding: 4px; background: #0c0f15; border: 1px solid var(--hairline, rgba(255,255,255,0.08)); border-radius: 14px; } .ds-tab { appearance: none; font-family: var(--font-ui, 'Space Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 14px; font-weight: 600; color: var(--muted, #8b95a5); background: transparent; border: 0; border-radius: 10px; min-height: 38px; padding: 0 16px; cursor: pointer; transition: background 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1), color 0.25s cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1); } .ds-tab:hover { color: var(--text, #e9edf4); } .ds-tab.ds-on { background: var(--panel-2, rgba(31,38,48,0.7)); color: var(--text, #e9edf4); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.06); }

components.name: Drive Pad
components.description: The on-screen joystick. A circular glass instrument with a gunsight crosshair marking zero and a gradient cap that tracks the thumb with no easing while held.
components.css: .ds-pad { --pad: 190px; width: var(--pad); height: var(--pad); position: relative; border-radius: 50%; background: radial-gradient(circle at 50% 38%, rgba(76,158,255,0.14), transparent 60%), var(--panel, rgba(19,24,33,0.72)); border: 1px solid var(--hairline-strong, rgba(255,255,255,0.14)); box-shadow: inset 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,0.06), 0 20px 50px -20px rgba(0,0,0,0.85); backdrop-filter: blur(20px) saturate(1.3); -webkit-backdrop-filter: blur(20px) saturate(1.3); touch-action: none; overflow: hidden; } .ds-pad-cross { position: absolute; inset: 0; pointer-events: none; } .ds-pad-cross::before, .ds-pad-cross::after { content: ''; position: absolute; background: var(--hairline, rgba(255,255,255,0.08)); } .ds-pad-cross::before { left: 12%; right: 12%; top: 50%; height: 1px; } .ds-pad-cross::after { top: 12%; bottom: 12%; left: 50%; width: 1px; } .ds-pad-ring { position: absolute; inset: 16%; border-radius: 50%; border: 1px dashed rgba(255,255,255,0.1); pointer-events: none; } .ds-pad-nub { position: absolute; left: 50%; top: 50%; width: 74px; height: 74px; margin: -37px 0 0 -37px; border-radius: 50%; background: linear-gradient(180deg, #7cc0ff, var(--accent-deep, #2f7fe0)); border: 1px solid rgba(255,255,255,0.35); box-shadow: 0 8px 20px -6px rgba(0,0,0,0.7), inset 0 1px 2px rgba(255,255,255,0.4); transition: transform 0.18s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-pad-label { position: absolute; bottom: 10px; left: 0; right: 0; text-align: center; font-family: var(--font-ui, 'Space Grotesk Variable', system-ui, sans-serif); font-size: 9px; letter-spacing: 0.2em; text-transform: uppercase; color: var(--faint, #5c6675); pointer-events: none; }

narrative.overview:
You are looking through a canopy at ground you are driving across, and the instruments are laid over it in machined glass. That is the whole system in one image. The map is never a panel in the layout — it is the world, full-bleed behind everything, and every control is a lens you read the world through rather than a card that replaces it. Panels blur and saturate what is behind them (blur(20px) saturate(1.3)), so the terrain stays legible through the glass and the operator never loses the connection between the numbers and the ground.

The surfaces are OLED-dark on purpose — near-black (#07090d) so an unlit pixel is genuinely off, and so the only things emitting light on the screen are the things that are actually happening. Chrome is quiet to the point of near-invisibility: hairlines at 8% white, labels at 22% letter-spacing in a grey you have to look for. What is loud is state. A live robot glows green. An armed e-stop breathes. A rejected setting paints its own left edge red. The interface holds still and lets the machines be the moving part.

Controls are tactile and consequential. Every press compresses (scale(0.96)), every transition uses a cubic-bezier with real mass and never a linear ease, and the drive nub tracks the finger with no transition at all while it is held — because a joystick that eases toward your thumb is a joystick that lies about what the robot is doing. Nothing here is decorative motion. Every animation is a machine acknowledging an instruction it is about to carry out.
keyCharacteristics: Full-bleed live map; all UI floats above it in translucent glass
Near-black OLED base with a rationed, signal-only palette
Two type voices: Space Grotesk for words, JetBrains Mono for anything a robot measured
No display type — the largest thing on screen is the word E-STOP at 17px
Raised glass for information, recessed wells for input
52px minimum tap target everywhere, on every screen size
Motion with mass; nothing linear, nothing decorative

rules.name: The Signal-Only Rule
rules.body: Green, amber, red and blue mean state and nothing else. No color is ever chosen because a surface looked plain. Audit test: point at any colored pixel and name the machine condition it reports — if you can't, it's wrong.

rules.name: The One Blue Rule
rules.body: Beacon Blue marks exactly one subject per view: the selected robot, or the state the machine is in right now. Two blue things competing in the same panel means the hierarchy has failed.

rules.name: The Big-Red-Is-Reserved Rule
rules.body: Exactly one element in the entire system is a large saturated fill: the E-STOP. Nothing else may take a solid red background, because the operator must be able to find it by color alone, at a glance, in a hurry.

rules.name: The No-Display Rule
rules.body: Nothing exceeds 17px. This is a console, not a page — there is no hero, no headline, and no title that announces where you are. If a new surface seems to need 32px type, it needs a better layout instead.

rules.name: The Mono-For-Measured Rule
rules.body: If a robot reported it, measured it, or a validator clamped it, it is JetBrains Mono. If a human wrote it, it is Space Grotesk. Never mix within one value.

rules.name: The Widely-Tracked-Small Rule
rules.body: Type below 11px is always uppercase and tracked to at least 0.1em. Small tight lowercase is unreadable at arm's length on a 7" panel in daylight.

rules.name: The Gap-Is-The-Map Rule
rules.body: The HUD's gutters are pass-through touch targets for the terrain. Never fill a gap with a background, and never add a full-bleed container behind the HUD grid.

rules.name: The Stop-Is-Never-Covered Rule
rules.body: The e-stop dock sits at z-index 1001; the settings sheet at 1000. Any new full-screen surface goes under the e-stop, and any layout that would push it off-screen is wrong. Changing a drive limit must never put the stop button out of reach.

rules.name: The Thumb-Floor Rule
rules.body: --tap: 52px is the minimum height for any primary control, and it does not shrink on the kiosk breakpoint. Controls that look smaller (the 44px gear) still carry a full tap target.

rules.name: The See-Through Rule
rules.body: Every floating panel is glass. A solid opaque panel over the map is a bug — the operator must always see the ground through the instruments. --panel-solid exists only for surfaces that are not over the map.

rules.name: The Float-Or-Sink Rule
rules.body: There is no flat surface in this system. A surface either floats (translucent + blur + bevel + drop shadow) or sinks (opaque #0c0f15 + hairline). If you are adding a surface and it is neither, decide which: does it present information, or does it receive input?

rules.name: The Glow-Is-Alive Rule
rules.body: A colored box-shadow means a live state — a lit LED, a filled calibration pip, an armed e-stop. Never apply a glow to a static surface for atmosphere.

rules.name: The Nested-Radius Rule
rules.body: A child's radius is always smaller than its parent's. 20 → 13 → 10 → 8. Never place a 20px-radius element inside a 13px one.

rules.name: The Round-Means-Live Rule
rules.body: Circles are reserved for things that move (nub, thumb, knob) or things that light up (LEDs, pips, badges). A circular static decoration does not exist here.

dos: Do float every panel on glass (rgba(19,24,33,0.72) + blur(20px) saturate(1.3) + a 1px rgba(255,255,255,0.06) top bevel). The terrain shows through the instruments — that is the system.
Do sink anything that receives input into an opaque #0c0f15 well with a hairline border. Float or sink; never flat.
Do set every number a robot reported in JetBrains Mono, and every word a human wrote in Space Grotesk.
Do keep every primary control at or above --tap: 52px, including on the 7" kiosk breakpoint.
Do put a control's state on its left-edge gutter (inset 2px 0 0 <signal>) so a column of fields reads as one status channel.
Do use --ease (cubic-bezier(0.32,0.72,0,1)) for state changes and --ease-out (cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1)) for things settling into place.
Do use linear transitions only for live measurements — telemetry bars, axis fills — where easing would misreport the machine.
Do honor prefers-reduced-motion — the system already collapses all durations to 0.001ms globally.
Do bundle every font and tile asset locally. There is no network in the field.
donts: Don't put a solid opaque panel over the map.
Don't use a signal color decoratively. If you can't name the machine condition a colored pixel reports, remove the color.
Don't give anything other than the E-STOP a large saturated red fill.
Don't let any element cover, scroll, or collapse the e-stop dock — it lives above every full-screen surface at z-index 1001.
Don't introduce display type. Nothing in this system exceeds 17px, and the largest type is the word E-STOP.
Don't ease the drive nub while it is being held. Zero lag under the thumb.
Don't add a parallel 4/8/12/16 spacing scale — the system runs on 3/6/9/14/16.
Don't rely on hover for anything. The primary device is a touchscreen with no pointer.
Don't fill the HUD's gutters with a background; they are how the operator touches the map.
Don't let this read as a consumer smart-home app, an enterprise SaaS dashboard, or a gamer/RGB aesthetic. All three are confirmed rejections.
